tips.comment: Skipped the Cheltenham Festival to come here fresh, which is exactly what he did last season as well. The yard stick the first time cheekpieces on this time. Whilst that may hint at the fact he's not straightforward, they did the same with State Man at the Cheltenham Festival. Everybody who watched that race knows barring his last flight fall, he would have won that Champion Hurdle comfortably. He ran at this meeting last season as mentioned above, winning the Aintree Hurdle over CD, beating Bob Olinger and Langer Dan in a 3-way go to the line. He's had 3 chase runs to date, winning a Novice Grade 1 2nd time out at Limerick. He ran okay last time out, beaten 10L in 3rd place behind Ballyburn and Croke Park. Leopardstown just isn't his track, so happy to overlook that run. I think he can reverse that form with Croke Park this time around.

Finished really strongly to win the Arkle Chase over 2 miles at last month's Cheltenham Festival. But will be far better suited by the step up in trip today, so is likely to improve again today and could take some beating.

Gidleigh Park is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Harry Fry and is 5/7 wins and 1/2 as a chaser, so clearly talented. He won last time out at Windsor in a Grade 2. He beat 4-6f favorite Caldwell Potter by a comfortable 4 lengths, a horse who has since won at the Cheltenham Festival, posting a career-high RPR of 157. Harry Fry and connections must be very excited about Gidleigh Park's chances and he has to enter calculations.

This horse looks overpriced for me. He won 2 Grade 1 novices, beating Heart Wood and then Betterdaysahead, and the form reads well. He was then 2nd to Ballyburn, beaten 5 lengths, with a further 5 lengths back to Impaire Et Passe. Yet that horse is much shorter here. This flat and speedier track should really suit him, and he's very hard to ignore at 4-1.
A 9 times career winner who has won 3 times this season, the last one over this trip at Kempton back in February, and looks an each-way player for a yard that does well here.

Won only two chase starts, travelling well before going clear in both races. Has won on good ground over hurdles. Looks to be an up-and-coming 7-year-old chaser. Remains to be seen if he's up to this level, but at 25/1, has to be worth an each-way punt.

This horse screams each way value to me to finish in the first 3 in this 9-runner race. The horse has more experience over fences than these, and one or two are ahead of his rivals in the betting. They have looked decidedly novicey in their jumping, and Aintree isn't the place to be making those mistakes. Boombawn only went down by a length to Rubaud last time out and gets a 5lb swing here, yet Rubaud is as short as 12/1 here. The favourite, Jango Baie, is the obvious danger (the other fancied ones in the betting have holes in them), but the favourite could be vulnerable since Nico over fences at Aintree doesn't particularly look like a match made in heaven to me.

Mark Of Gold is a big price for the opener here but arrives in good form with stats of 2-1-3-3-1 and having won in this class before could give a good account here at a value price for each way backers.

I wouldn't give this horse a prayer of getting a fast run 2 miles based on his pedigree, but he did it on his head in the Fred Winter and was so impressive it is very hard not to see him winning again. For a flat-bred horse, he has got quite some size and physique, and he could be a bit of a freak.

Murcia is a 4yo filly trained by Willie Mullins and ridden by stable jockey Paul Townend. She ran respectably at the Cheltenham Festival and previously finished 2/7 at Naas, beaten a neck by the extremely useful Bacchanalian (level weights), who has won on his next start at Naas in a Grade 3 contest by 11 lengths. The third, Ephesus, 8 lengths behind, has since won a big field maiden at Limerick to frank the form further. Today, Murcia receives a 7lb filly allowance, which could prove to be pivotal, and the fact Paul Townend chooses Murcia speaks volumes.

Behind Puturhandstogether at Cheltham, giving it weight and will do well to turn the form around. But it didn't have the best of trips that day, and I think it ran better than its finishing position. Could be the main danger to the favorite.

Fairly smart flat pedigree and readily dispatched a fair 138 rated horse two starts back. Less good last time, although was conceding weight to two horses who acquitted themselves well in the Triumph. Held back since that run in December, he could find something extra for the return to better ground on the balance of his flat form. I’d hope that Live Conti has some of these out of their comfort zone enough for something to pick up the pieces up the straight.

I think Skelton usually brings on his new runners markedly, so it's not beyond the realms of capability that LIVE CONTI goes close, and he harbors a good chance here. It was a tasty 3yo race victory in Auteuil on debut, and the easy win at Wetherby loosened him up to life racing here. One to keep tabs on.
Probably doesn't have enough experience over jumps to win this, but he was really impressive on his winning debut last time and was a particularly slick jumper. Worth an each-way punt.

Was firmly put in his place in the Triumph when pulled up and under pressure 3 out and pulled up before the last hurdle. Put that form well and truly behind him, winning the Adonis at Kempton when staying on strongly and is given another chance each way at big odds.

Despite Pulling Up in latest run, Gibbs Island has improved with each run and is one of the few that has appeal in what is a difficult race. He usually starts off well and should be in the final frame. Should stay on and could be a solid contender.
Another excellent horse from the Mullins yard with the excellent Rachel Blackmore on board. So, over an ideal distance, could be well placed today.
A decent jumper who should have no problem getting the distance. With the excellent booking of Harry Cobden, it should be there or thereabouts at the finish. Looking like a great bet to place.

In terms of quality, this is one of the weaker races on the card, so it may be worth opposing the favorite at such short odds and taking a chance elsewhere. GIVE IT TO ME OJ has been steadily improving and could be worth an each-way chance at the price. Looks to improve again for a try at Aintree, and let's not forget it cost £100,000 and is pretty well related to benefit from today's conditions. Always a risk, but certainly the race where I can see an upset. Small stakes for this one, but can certainly get involved with improvement likely.
Something of an unknown quantity, but this seems like an open race. Coconut Grove won last September in France over 1.4f. Up in trip today, but could be a surprise entity.

Terrorise is chanced each way on hurdling debut for Brian Ellison in this juvenile hurdle. The stable does quite well with unexposed outsider types. The 4yo is by Territories with Galileo in the pedigree on the dam's side and won on the Flat on handicap debut over ten furlongs. Three lengths winner on that occasion at a big price (22-1). Hasn't shown any other form to note but is intriguing dropped in for hurdles debut at this Grade 1 level.
This drying ground will suit Grey Dawning who was impressive last time at Kelso after being freshened up since his hard race at Haydock.

Spillane's Tower is a 7-year-old gelding trained by James Joseph Mangan, bred by Mrs. Noreen McManus, and owned by J.P. McManus, so it's a real family affair. Spillane's Tower has 4 out of 9 wins since he's been sent chasing, posting a career-high RPR of 166, so he's very talented. He was disappointing in the King George at Kempton but is clearly held in high regard, being sent off as the 11-4 favorite. Three starts back, he beat the 160-rated Monty's Star under today's jockey, Mark Walsh, a jockey of the highest standard. Spillane's Tower stays this trip, is ground versatile, and is one of the likeliest candidates in today's field to take home this valuable prize.

Ahoy Senor has a great record at this track. He has never been out of the first three in six runs here, including two wins. He has been running well in this race for the last two years. He goes well on the expected ground here, and the 10-year-old looks worth another chance in this, after falling when in front at Cheltenham three weeks ago.
GAELIC WARRIOR's best hurdling performance was over the longer trip, and he seems a perfectly capable chaser now. So, throwing this longer trip into the equation seems to make sense.

STAGE STAR may have hinted latest he is ready to come to hand. Presumably jockey Harry Cobden would have confirmed this classy chaser is suited by the more extreme distances from his last start and so likely set aside by trainer Paul Nicholls who often targets this meeting he should be competitive.

A few tempters in here, in what looks perhaps more of an open race than it looks on paper, but especially when you consider the highest-rated horse in here is actually the outsider, which is surely a rarity. Embassy Gardens I just felt was overpriced coming out of the Irish Gold Cup, where the form speaks for itself. Interestingly, he’s fresh for this off a 90+ day break, and with him being 3/3 a place with 2 wins off breaks bigger than 120 days, freshness could be the key for his effort. He’s Townend's pick too, which adds a positive, with Paul being 3/5 aboard. The ground is a real unknown, which is a hint perhaps to his price, but I’m not convinced they’d be running here if they didn’t expect him to take to it.

I'm going to plump for Djelo, whose odds I think are a bit too big. Currently 25/1. Three places on offer in this 8-runner race. I'm going to forgive his last run at Cheltenham and hope that something was just amiss that day, as before that he was running very well. His form figures actually read 71212. He might go well at big odds.

If The Real Whacker avoids early mistakes, he could be prominent throughout at Aintree. He was unfortunate to have to play catch-up in the Cheltenham Gold Cup after a blunder at the first, but then eventually led and made another mistake at the 17th before weakening into 5th.

Constitution Hill won this race comfortably in 2023 and should not have a problem with the extra distance against Lossiemouth, who probably prefers this distance. Despite Constitution Hill's fall at Cheltenham, he is a more reliable and fluent jumper than Lossiemouth. In 2023, he showed exceptional pace around Aintree to make all.

Lossiemouth was one of the most impressive winners of the Mares Hurdle at Cheltenham for many years. Will prefer this 2m4f trip to the 2 miles at Kempton when the mare only found Constitution Hill 2.5 lengths too good. Can reverse placings now. Receives a 7 pounds mares allowance here. Jockey Paul Townend and Willie Mullins in top form each with 8 winners from last 12 runners.

The roughies in here could do any sort of spoiling by going too hard, or not going fast enough. So whilst it should be a fairly straightforward matchup between the front two, as we’ve seen recently, anything goes in these races. Wodhooh has been lightly raced this campaign, perhaps with an eye for this race, and she’s been a ready winner in two competitive handicaps so far. She looked to have won both with more in hand than was perhaps obvious, going away from the field on both occasions without being completely reached for. She’ll get no such luxury in a small field, but with a habit of getting her head down and nose in front, I think she’s a fair price to hit the two should one or the other of the principals falter.

This selection's best effort to date was a 3rd place finish over the distance of 20 furlongs in a Group 1. Racing over the distance of 20 furlongs in today's contest, the ground should suit. Harry Skelton is retained and has each-way appeal (if one of the top two in the betting falls or fails to finish).

Last month's Champion Hurdle showed that anything can happen when the top hurdlers jump at top speed. Break My Soul is an enormous price for a runner who is consistent, will enjoy running on the fast ground and looks to have been aimed at the race. I am hoping he can stay on and pinch second place.

I backed Willitgoahead at Cheltenham and I felt he was given too much to do. Held up, most of the market leaders he jumped great but had to make up too much ground. That hard race could have left its mark, and I'm very keen on Lifetime Ambition. He knows his way around here, having finished 4th before and also was running a cracker in the Grand National when trained by Jessica Harrington but got taken out by a loose horse. I feel like this is a long-term plan to be laid out for this by his shrewd hunter trainer and has one of the best amateur riders on board, and there's tons to like.

Willitgoahead has a big shout in the Foxhunters. Stayed on to finish third in the Foxhunters at Cheltenham only beaten three and a half lengths there. Strong form coming into this race. Trained by Gordon Elliott and solidly backed ahead of this hunter chase on second run for the stable.

My Drogo showed he still was a classy performer in winning his first hunter chase at Haydock. He lost form after being injured when with Dan Skelton after winning here over hurdles against Minella Dream in 2021. He also won at Cheltenham that year over fences. He was off for nearly two years and disappointed in the Old Roan Chase here in 2023. He left Dan Skelton after pulling up in an Exeter hurdle in 2024 but could be close to the top in hunter chases.

Won a point-to-point race last month at Cothelstone, and that was over three miles. I do think the two-mile and five-furlong distance at Aintree will be the perfect setup. With three wins in the last five races, I think Famous Clermont can prove his class by winning this Foxhunters Open Hunters Chase.

A past winner of 3 point races who has shown improved form to win 2 Hunter Chases from 2 starts, both in good style for his current trainer, who could hardly be in better form at the moment. Looks to be improving and looks a big player.

JOKER DE MAI has clearly been aimed specificaly at this race this time around as mentioned by classy trainer Harry Derham. Owner/jockey David Maxwell would be a jockey with more experience than most lining up for this renewal and as a younger type his chance appears clear.

Like a lot of these in this year's Foxhunters, if you look back far enough in the form book, their rating is far higher than the current mark. That is exactly what can be said of Presentandcounting, as his current mark is 122, but looking back to 2022, his mark was 21lb higher at 143. That is some difference for one that I feel still has ability. Likes to be prominent (no bad thing here to stay out of trouble) as he has shown the last twice only to weaken late on over 24/25f. The drop back in trip here to 21f should suit, and with Derek O'Connor in the saddle again (was last time), I'm hoping he can go well. Having Derek in the plate can prove vital as he is the most successful point-to-point rider of all time, and along with the name McCain (synonymous with these national fences), my selection looks great value at huge odds.

GRACCHUS DE BALME looks seriously overpriced in this race. He finished 2nd behind My Drogo at Haydock, giving him 6 lbs. They're off level weights here, so there's a chance of regarding the form. The selection was a disappointing favorite when pulled up on heavy ground at Leicester latest. Assuming he's over that issue, he can definitely outrun his odds.
Bennys King is another who has run well in the past over these big national-style fences. He has performed well this season over fences and should be competitive in this prestigious hunter chase.

This selection's best effort to date was a 3rd place finish (in this race last year) over the distance of 21 furlongs. It drops back down to race over 21 furlongs in today's contest. Hopeful the ground will suit. Mr. P W Mullins is retained. Has each-way appeal, yet hopeful it can go close.
A big price each-way chance who has inconsistent form and pulled up last time at Leicester, but the trip was inadequate and should be more suited by 2m5f today.

Took third place behind the re-opposing My Drogo at Haydock over a slightly longer trip in February. Likes to be up with the pace, which can be an advantage in races on the national course over shorter distances. Has a more experienced rider on board today and looks a massive price for each-way purposes, with many bookies paying out on extra places.

I'm going to get on early at this price, 50/1, for a good each way with plenty of places up for grabs. Ramillies, a sound jumper, should relish this over this shorter distance and going it will like. B O'Neil rides for consistent trainer D Christie.

Evas Oskar can go well for the Vaughan yard. Evas Oskar ran a very good race in the Grand National at this track in 2023 and was second at Catterick last time out. He has won over this trip before and can do well today.

Distance Winner was made favourite for his last run but finished behind one of today's rivals, Captain Tommy. He was staying on one pace at the finish of 2m 4f on good going, so today's slightly longer trip of 2m 5f 19yds should suit. Speculative each-way bet @66/1 paying 5 places.

Percussion looks a solid each way bet, with an outstanding record in top handicaps over these National fences - form figures 3-3-2-3-7. He hasn't threatened on either start in the hunter chase sphere so far, but a return to this C&D can see him regain his best form, which should see him in the frame. Presentandcounting looks another that can outrun his odds under Derek O'Connor, with the step back in trip and his forward-going style both likely to suit in a race where so many have nicked it off the front.

This selection's best effort to date was a 2nd place finish over the distance of 26.5 furlongs in a class 2. Racing around 21 furlongs in today's contest, the ground should suit. Mr. C Mullins is retained and has each-way appeal.

JJ O'Shea trained the winner of this race in 2021 at a whopping price of 66/1. He runs Willewonga here at a big price, and arriving on the back of some solid form, could go well here at a winning distance and ground that will suit.

This 9-year-old is a solid option, having come in 2nd, 8 1/2 lengths behind Bennys King, in a hunter chase at Leicester 37 days ago. With odds of 50/1, he presents a good opportunity for an each-way bet that could be quite profitable.

Senior Citizen has run well over these fences in the past. Was formerly trained by Alan King and took well to these fences. Won a point recently in impressive fashion and represents each-way value in an open-looking race.
Bardenstown Lad ran too freely in its last race and threw away any chance early on. It won its two races prior to that. This shorter distance may help it further to get a place.

My Mate Mozzie ran a solid race when 4th of 20 at Cheltenham. The drying ground will improve his good chance in this. Trip is ideal and if he reproduces his last run then he has a winning opportunity.

Both stable and jockey seem to be in sync of late, and they'll have their eyes on a follow-up win at the Aintree Festival after a success at Cheltenham. PRIMOZ has a good chance of getting close today.
Was a smooth winner 2 runs back and then sent off just 5-2 to follow up. He got brought down and has been kept for this. If he can stay out of trouble, I think he's fairly weighted to go very close.

Sans Bruit flew from the start in this race last year and made all under Bryony Frost. Harry Cobden is likely to try the same tactics again, as the horse obviously enjoyed the Mildmay Course. Nothing got close to him from out of the handicap to register his only UK win so far.

This horse comes here fresher than most, and the trainer's horses have been running better in the last few weeks. Some recent winners of this had come here having had a quiet campaign and basically avoided running on bad ground, and the trainer's patience can pay off here. He's won this race twice in the last 5 years with the same jockey, and this will no doubt have been the plan for some time. Looks to have the ideal profile and is a win at class 1, unlike some of those ahead of him in the market.
Rath Gaul Hill is out of the handicap here but could still be improving as he has won his last three handicap chases including first time out this season when ridden by Sam Twiston-Davies at Newbury.

Dan Skelton trained Calico was a winner over 2 miles here in October on similarly good ground. Beat some useful sorts including Matata from a mark of 138. Has continued to run well and has good place claims. May appreciate being back at a course he has winning form at. Could be decently handicapped still on a mark of 140. Harry Skelton rides.

For the each-way value, it was a close choice between him and the Evan Williams horse who has beaten him. But on the likely ground, this horse actually has the beating of a lot of these on collateral form. Whether this comes too soon, who knows?

This distance winner is joint top rated on 152 (down from 155 last time out). He finished a not too bad 4th of 9 last time out 33 days ago in a class 2 after making smooth headway 3 out and plugging on after the last. Has wins on good and good to soft so drying ground should suit with Danny McMenamin who has won on him before returning to the saddle.

Gunsight Ridge arrives here off the back of a career-best performance at Sandown, a top-tier Grade 1 track, where he ran prominently throughout and always looked to be doing enough in a valuable Class 2 hunters’ chase. While his two runs prior to that weren’t much to go off, his latest effort suggests he’s coming back to form at the right time. A proven performer at Aintree, he won over course and distance in 2022 and has even gone off as festival favourite here before. With solid track form and strong ratings on my figures, he looks well worth a chance at the current odds. Good luck!

GALUNGGUNG still low-mileage satisfies some trends for this race and there was something to like about the way jockey Brian Hughes saved something when this now progressive nine year old last won. He may have been spying this race on the back of that effort , so in a renewal which frames in our favour from an each-way perspective he rates a player.
5 places and 1 win in 9 races at a similar going. Rides under Tom Broughton for the first time today and riding in a larger field today for the first time. 50/1 appeals for each way.

This selection's best effort to date was a 5th place finish over the distance of 16 furlongs in a Group 1. Racing over the distance of 15.5 furlongs in today's contest, hopeful the ground will suit. J J Slevin is in the saddle and has each-way appeal.

I would really like this horse to get a famous win here after an excellent season that has seen it win 2 races. Numping is much better these days and traveling much more sweetly. The horse is up five pounds for its last run but will love this big field.
Seo Linn comes to Aintree fresh, having not run since winning comfortably in a Listed bumper at Cheltenham in November. Her second bumper win looks the best form on paper here.

Charisma Cat has a strong record of 3 wins from 4 starts, including a victory at Sandown. She was unlucky at Market Rasen, and her consistent form suggests she is a big player in this race. With plenty of potential, she could be a serious contender for the win here.

JACKIE HOBBS runs for a trainer who has potential for a good meeting this year. Taking on her own sex she has shown improved form in her two Bumper wins to date and syndicate owned she would likely be a runner who attracts support on the day. Decent each-way claims.

I'll cover the favorite of Paddy Twomey and a good each way on the now ridden by Harry Cobden, Kapability. Won here on debut with plenty of winners emerging from that since. Looks a solid play for Honeyball.

This horse couldn't have been any more impressive when well supported at 7/4 and hacking up after travelling like a dream. We have seen in these last few weeks how Fergal O'Brien has been keeping his powder dry rather than firing it all at Cheltenham, and this has been the target race for this horse since that easy success on her sole start. She's by the same sire as Constitution Hill which isn't too shabby and the current fav (Seo Linn) is by a sire not known for putting ones trust in so we are getting an inflated price partly on that basis. Certainly looks the e/w value at 9/1.
Looked very impressive when winning at Warwick in lower class but couldn't have won in better style. Needs to improve again but is in capable hands and is interesting at a big price.

La Conquiere showed plenty of promise on debut, finishing second with a strong tactical run. Trainer Jamie Snowden believes in her potential, and Gavin Sheehan adds big-race experience. As a mature six-year-old, she could thrive in the demanding conditions of this Grade 2 contest.

Stable in good form, and this was 5l behind Seo Linn at the Paddy Power meeting. It improved from that run to show good qualities to win a class 2 bumper at Warwick. Looks good value here with her experience crucial.
Has run well on all 4 bumper starts to date, having placed in both of the first 2 starts and winning the last 2 races. Should go well again in hat-trick attempt and holds an each-way chance at least.

This is very competitive and it is not often you can get 16/1 about a Skelton runner in a bumper. The anticipated fast pace should suit as she is by an Old Vic mare so there is plenty of stamina in the pedigree.

Oldschool Outlaw comes in with strong form, including two solid runner-up finishes and clear progression. Her RPR of 119 is among the best in the field, and she’s proven to be game in tight finishes. Trainer Garry Caldwell has handled her smartly, and she could surprise if she keeps improving.

Finished second to a stablemate who re-opposes here last time. However, my pick was giving him 4 lbs and now doesn't have to, and there was hardly anything between them. That form should be reversed, and the pick is very unexposed. The trainer has won this race before.

La Zoubida, trained by Nicky Richards, whose charge is sired by Authorized, has a pedigree that can see speed and a turn of foot appearing. He showed his ability at Market Rasen when quickening when his jockey asked. Sean Quinlan has kept the ride, and we could be seeing a big run appearing with this ground playing to his strengths. Pray they do not do the over-watering.

While St Irene has finished behind some of these rivals in Listed events, she has shown some potential with consistent form. At odds of 33/1, she could offer some value if she manages to find improvement and take a step forward in this competitive field.

ST JESSICA creates some interest as a runner from a yard who appear to have done well to secure the services of Rachael Blackmore. Presumably Ireland's ace rider would have been under consideration for other mounts in this race and this daughter of Malinas could take at least as big a step forward as many others second-up.

There are not many trainers in such good form as Killahena & McPherson (3 from 3 in last 14 days) and they run Amelia's Star who can go well at huge odds. Saw the track for the first time in Nov when coming from the back to finish a promising 2nd of 11 (winner won again since). Not seen then until late Jan when running out a nice winner 1st of 9 beating one that has gone on and won again. She has had plenty of time to come on again and with the yard flying this one is not without a chance.

It remains to be seen how Handstands will perform on faster conditions at Aintree. He won his only point and won his first hurdle race on good going. This season, switching to fences, he fell in his first chase but has then been unbeaten in his last three races: two Grade 2 novice chases and last time a battling short-head win over Jango Baie at Sandown in a Grade 1 novice chase. He could win again.

Caldwell Potter can go well for the Paul Nicholls yard. Caldwell Potter won very well at Cheltenham last time out and never looked like losing, jumping very well in that run. Can do better again and should go well on this ground.

Handstands is a warm favorite for this race and rightly so. Trends tend to favor those who ran at Cheltenham last time out. This lad fits the bill. He actually won at this meeting last season too, winning the Sefton Novices very comfortably, putting 5 lengths between himself and the runner-up, The Jukebox Man, at the finish, having traveled into the race like a very good thing. Admittedly, he needs to overcome a poor run in the Brown Advisory. He never seemed to enjoy himself on that occasion, so happy to draw a line through that run and give him another chance. He was 2/2 over fences prior to the last run, with the Grade 3 win being the pick of those efforts. He made all the running, jumped brilliantly, and was always in command. If he can repeat that run here, I think he can put it up to the favorite.

Unlike most in this, it will definitely get the trip as the last 4 runs have all been at around this distance. One thing it probably won't get is the testing conditions that favor it. It has been 2nd on the last 2 runs at Navan and 23 days ago in the Brown Advisory, beaten 4L with 2 of today's rivals further behind.

I think in this field it looks the second most likely winner due to its potential, staying ability, enthusiasm, and its fantastic jumping ability. I've got a value price of 9/2 down, and Ladbrokes are offering a warm 9/2 on the horse. Looks, in my opinion, the best bet by a mile. Hanstands will be hard to beat, and Don't Rightly Know's trainer is currently out of form. But I still believe it has the 2nd best chance, and being the outsider of the field is just too big in my opinion. Should definitely be shorter on the off.

This horse was backed off the boards to land the ultra-competitive Martin Pipe race at the end of the Cheltenham Festival but flopped there. However, it is still unexposed and is clearly thought to be much better than that. I suspect early mistakes ruined his confidence, and maybe the 'lesser' jockey didn't give the horse the best ride on the day. So he's well worth another chance with Mark Walsh now in the saddle. For any horse to go off as short as 5/2 in the Martin Pipe on his fifth start, you'd have to say he's very highly thought of. Any horse is usually worth forgiving for one poor run, so the 13/2 is well worth taking.

Handicapper has left his mark untouched for the last run. To be fair, he stood little chance being ridden out wide throughout. Still, he travelled into contention before his run petered out. I still think he's well in off this type of mark based on his overall form. The trainer has saddled 2 of the last 3 winners of this race, so knows what it takes to win this event. His run behind Burdett Road in the Greatwood rates the standout piece of form. He was only beaten 1/2L by that horse. That form got boosted with Burdett Road finishing 2nd in the Champion Hurdle a few weeks back. If he repeats that form here, that would give him decent claims.

Another trainer who tends to target his runners at this race, having won this 3 times in the past. He ran a cracker in the Coral Cup last time out, sporting the first-time cheekpieces. He travelled into the race like the winner but was eventually run down late on by another of Willie Mullins' handicap good things in Jimmy Du Seuil. No disgrace there given that horse was massively chucked in off his handicap debut mark. The handicapper has reacted accordingly, shoving him up 4 lbs for that run, which means he must shoulder top weight in this race. His overall form would suggest he should be able to cope with the rise in the weights. He won well enough on his penultimate run at Newbury, again travelling into the race like a good thing, recording a nice easy win in the end. If he repeats that run and the Coral Cup run, he's probably the one to beat here if the weight concession isn't a problem for him.

The 6yo has 3 wins from 5 over hurdles. Tricky to weigh up the form from his last race, a 19L novice hurdle win. He’s best judged on his second start, on good ground, when a close second in an introductory hurdle race, splitting two smart rivals. His opening handicap mark looks handy. Strong jockey in the saddle.

WRECKLESS ERIC is likely a runner better suited by this flat track and the extra distance. The Imperial Cup at Sandown may be a decent season-long guide and this mildly progressive five year old representing the O'Neill trainer combination should be in the mix.

Steel Ally arrives in top form after a narrow second to Nemean Lion in a valuable Class 1, Grade 2 race at Fontwell, posting career-best figures in both performance and speed. That run came over a left-handed, sharp track similar to Aintree, making this a suitable test. Two starts back, he tackled a shorter 2-mile trip but lacked the speed to feature, while three runs ago, he secured a solid 3-length victory carrying 11st 11lb. His consistency, proven ability to improve with class, and strong showing in one of the most competitive races last time out make him a compelling contender here. Good luck!

Won 3 on the bounce on Good and Good to Soft. Followed that up with 4L 4th in a Listed contest and 4th in a G2. Has form behind Diva Luna in Listed and G2 Bumper, and that's worked out well. Harry Atkins takes off 7lb in a race the Skeltons have won 2 of the last 3.

Never discount these silks at Aintree. This one has some good course form after finishing 2nd to Jingo Baie in The Tolworth in December 2023. The tip has failed to trouble the judge in 3 runs this season from 15.5-16.5f and has never run over today's 20f trip, but I'll take a chance.
Expensive purchase Off The Jury is still a Maiden over hurdles, however, he has ran some cracking races in defeat. He could run very well at a stand-out 25/1 with bet365.

Blenkinsop was absent for 659 days after running in a three-mile Grade 1 novice hurdle at this Meeting in 2023 but looked to be coming back into form in his second race back at Uttoxeter last time when 3rd of 15 over this distance, beaten less than five lengths. If he comes on again for that run, he could go close at 50-1.

A typically tricky contest, and there are a few of interest that would have been primed for Cheltenham and may struggle to post their best efforts just three weeks later. Brentford Hope skipped Cheltenham and has been running in Graded company the last twice, first when behind Constitution Hill and then LTO last of four in the Kingwell. He was disappointing when last seen in handicap company, finishing down the field at Windsor, but that's a bit of a funny track, so I'm happy to forgive him that effort. He's undoubtedly well handicapped on the evidence of his Punchestown run last spring when finishing 2nd to Daddy Long Legs when giving that rival 8lbs, who has since won a Grade 3 and is now rated 151. I like spring festival form and big field handicap form, with Brentford Hope bringing both to the table, and a mark of 141 is 2lbs lower than his Punchestown run. He steps up in trip for the first time but seemed to see out 17f up the Cheltenham hill well enough in the Unibet Hurdle, and if the extra distance finds any improvement, he should be right in the mix.
Beacon Edge ran respectably when 7th in the Coral Cup at the Cheltenham Festival. Looks fairly handicapped, and the return to this easier track should suit.

Minella Missile is very well weighted on the best of his form. He has lost his form somewhat this season, but carries a low weight, and if anywhere near the level of ability when beating Captain Teague, he could make a mockery of these huge odds.

Not exactly a great price for this race, but I feel he's a solid choice given he ran a cracker in the Supreme Novices last time out. That race is usually a good prep for this one, with 9 of the last 12 winners of this running in the Supreme prior to coming here and taking this race. He's proven to be a useful horse this season. Form figures 1213. Winning his maiden on hurdling debut with any amount in hand. He managed to win the Grade 1 Paddy Power Novices on his penultimate run, beating stablemate Bleu De Vassy with any amount in hand. As mentioned above, he finished 3rd in the Supreme last time out. He ran very well, just couldn't match the finishing speed of the front two. He did stay on nicely enough, however. If he repeats that form here, he's the one to beat for me. He's a confident selection.

Diva Luna won a bumper at this meeting last year, but her only hurdles win so far was in a maiden hurdle against geldings at Cheltenham on New Year's Day over two and a half miles. She finished 3rd of 23 last time at the Cheltenham Festival in a Grade 2 mares' novice hurdle over two miles one furlong. Could at least get a place, getting her seven-pound mares' allowance.

Arrives here off a mark of 137 and is improving every run. Won the last two, firstly at Ayr over 16f on soft in January, and then 34 days ago at Kelso, winning Grade 2 Novice Hurdle on good to soft over 18f with the fancied W. Mullins' favourite 2.5L behind in 2nd. Drops back 2f in trip today shouldn't be a problem.
This horse won impressively by 14 lengths off a mark of 72 at this course three outings ago. It clearly enjoys this track and remains a contender worth considering.
Failed to complete only previous chase when pulling up at Worcester 3 years ago. Not seen since finishing 4th of 10 over hurdles a year ago. Each way chance if finding that form on return to action.

Blacksamsenorita looks the obvious selection here. Choice of all 12 pro tipsters. Comfortable winner at odds on last time by 12 lengths, making all at Exeter. In-form trainer Joe Tizzard (SR 24%). By Black Sam Bellamy, this 6yo should have no problem stepping up to 2m4f. Rivals don't have as promising form over hurdles.
Leading Swoop comes into this one today after a decent last run win mid last month. Looking like the one to catch.
This horse likely needed the outing when finishing third, beaten by 22 lengths, in a handicap chase at Fontwell in its latest run, where the heavy ground didn't suit. Could bounce back.
Totally unreliable sort, but has a win here on decent ground and is far enough down the handicap these days to take a chance on him bouncing back to form.

Improving 4-year-old who hacked up here on penultimate start before winning more cosily than the margin suggested at Sandown LTO on handicap debut. 5 lbs higher here, but the step up in trip should unlock more potential, and the runner-up at Sandown has run well since.
Fav hasn't run over this far yet. Selection won well over course and distance last time, and the 5lb rise in weights looks more than fair. Chance of following up here.
In its latest outing, this horse finished third in a handicap hurdles over 2 miles 3 furlongs at Carlisle, where it encountered traffic problems. Major player.

Masterpiece has had a break since winning a bumper at Newcastle. He is locally trained by Rebecca Menzies, and if well-schooled for his first hurdle race, he should have enough pace to win in this moderate field.

This one was trained by Gordon Elliott in Ireland but failed to win 10 hurdle races from 16 to 21.8f. He was dropped to 16f on debut for the present stable when 2L 2nd for this team and goes up 1lb back up to 19.8f. Worth another try to improve and win for the current stable.
Ex Skelton horse. Still going okay when falling two out last time. Looks a trappy race and at 50s, could well outrun his odds. Worth a small speculative each way bet.
Hurdles winner at Southwell in February and followed that with a 2nd at Bangor over fences. Should go well again and likely to be there or thereabouts.
Tom Creen is a course specialist here and has won five times here. He was a close second last time out. Hard to oppose here and should be competitive with a chance to make it number six.

Beat 4 lengths over course and distance off this mark on penultimate start, ridden by Brian Hughes, and has Emma Smith-Chaston in the saddle today claiming a 3-pound allowance that could prove valuable.

Last 2 starts, both over hurdles, have been poor, but its best form is over fences. Not faring too badly on its last chase start, 3 starts back, when only being beaten by 4 1/2L over 20f at Worcester (Class 5) on good ground. Hasn't scored for a while (wins coming in Ireland) but carries its lowest weight since 2021. The trainer is 2 from 3 (67%) with chasers, and his charge is top-rated in some quarters. Outsider of the pack (28/1 best price) but could go well today.

Still a maiden over hurdles after eight runs. However, has three wins and three seconds from only ten starts on the flat when trained in France, so definitely not without ability. Interesting that the last six runs have been in handicaps, and today goes back into a maiden and drops in trip on this quicker ground where his flat speed will come to the fore. Has far more race experience than today's rivals, having already racked up £40K of win and place prize money. My best bet of the day.

Was in the process of running well with a chance of winning when blundered the final hurdle and faded into third place. Lost a shoe in the process and looked unlucky. On just the second start here, could improve to beat this field barring any bad mistakes. First runner at this track for the trainer who sends this 4-year-old 250 miles for this test.

The only mare in the field, Ann D'arabie, off a lowly mark of 78, has a good chance of overcoming course winner Old Page. Old Page may find the eight-pound rise for his latest win slowing him down at the finish, whilst Ann D'arabie showed promise when 2nd at Doncaster in her first chase, and her mark was kept at 78.
Sedgefield regular Old Page won again here last time out over this trip 2 weeks ago, and again on good ground, is a major player.
Already been hammered in the betting but still worth a go at 9/1. It's almost now or never for the horse being on such a low mark at 12 years old.
Shaped well last time, doing best of those held up and ran on well into 4th. Of interest here as he is dropped in grade, significantly from a class 2 into a class 5.

The Wise Traveller has immediately caught my attention here was last seen over this course and distance 14 days ago where finishing 4th/6 however he has slipped off the handicappers radar and is now operating on a mark of 93 that being 5lb below his last winning mark and must be taken seriously in a race of this nature jockey K Brogan takes the ride on Mrs S J Humphrey's gelded son of Getaway and can give this his best shot must be considered
Disappointing effort last time out. Easing in weights and also dropping in grade could revive his form. If he gets the lead, he can win.
Strongly supported when winning by 3.25 lengths off a mark of 88 at Huntingdon. Trainer currently in good form. Solid claims.

A race where the market leaders should dominate. Micky Hammond's Milajess has been the bridesmaid in her last three races but it is time to take her place as the bride with the ground conditions perfect for her. I expect the blinkers on 2nd time around to bring about enough improvement to beat Trailblazer who himself has had a wind op but this may not take effect until his next race.

Balranald CD winner, good to soft and even better 2m1f winner last October. Consistent since, and the latest run came after a 99-day break. Should benefit from that run and has every chance of landing a 3rd course win in this.
Didn't achieve much on the flat but has had wind surgery since he ran 46 days ago, and that could make a huge difference here. Each way player.
Ran very strongly here in November when a close 2nd. This looks like a slightly lower class of horses. If it gets away clean, it could take all the beating. EW value.
Distance winner and only 1 lb above last winning mark. Had also won here at Chelmsford. Very solid each way chance. Stall 5 will help get a good position early on.

Forest Haze has dropped another 3lbs since his last run and is now 13lbs below his opening handicap mark, so he’s starting to look dangerously well treated. With a 7lb claimer booked today, he’s effectively running off a career-low mark and could go well if things click.

CRACKING FILLY saves what best she has to offer for this venue and this race is a near-basement grade handicap where she can be given realistic claims. She comes from Dean Ivory's yard who can land touches in the low grade races with one from his string and she can be considered.
Stintino Sunset makes his stable debut. He was a consistent performer when with William Stone including a course and distance win and could do well if settled in.
12 runs to date and no wins. Did not look close to winning LTO when 7 of 8 at Southwell last month, but has course experience and has performed well here in the past.

Paradoxical won 4 in a row at Wolverhampton in February and March before finishing 2nd at the same venue 10 days ago. He is up another 2lbs and runs for the first time at Chelmsford but looks to have a great chance of going in again.
Has run well in 2 of his last 3 runs. Though it's more than 2 years since his last win, he ran his best race for ages last time. His turn could be near as he is well in on old form.

Curran’s form dipped after a decent third at Ayr last summer, but he’s had a wind operation since and returns off a much-reduced mark, now 13 lbs lower than his opening one. The drop back to 10f should suit better, and the yard has a good record with all-weather runners fresh (167 runs, 37 wins, 22% strike rate, +40 pts @ 24% ROI). If the operation has done the trick, he could go well at a nice price.

This looks the perfect race for Cavalry Call to get his head back in front was last seen at Kempton at the 1 mile trip where finishing a creditable 6th/13 steps up in trip here tackling the 1 mile 2 furlong trip for the first time that most certainly being a positive move by his connections as he has shown signs in past races that this trip is well worth exploring with this gelded son of Invincible Spirit currently operating on a mark of 73 it is very well possible he is a step ahead of the handicapper and is likely to have much bigger performance in the locker just waiting to be unleashed in very good time jockey Jack Mitchell takes the ride on Simon & Ed Crisford's inmate an can give him the perfect ride here at Chelmsford merits serious consideration
Kodiac filly. Dam smart over 6f at 2 years old. Should have plenty of speed. Cheekpieces on, so that could be a concern, but yard in form.
Could nick the race from the front here. Close 2nd the last twice and comes here off the same mark, so has a big chance here.
3 times a winner over 6 furlongs here and a beaten favourite over that trip here last month. Yet to win over 5 furlongs in 7 attempts but has finished runner-up over course and distance.

Last outing can be ignored when 9/10 due to bad luck at the start with a poor draw and raced wide until he failed to get back inside at the first time of asking. His running stats suggest that 5f is his trip, and he runs off 60 once more. If he can get in position early, he has a really good chance here.
Bred in the Purple won well on Polytrack twice last year. Didn't handle the heavy ground in GP1 Futurity last time, but this is a massive drop in class and should win on the snaff.

Yaroogh looks a really nice type and nearly landed a Group 3 at Newbury last time, just racing a bit too keenly late on. That came off the back of a solid nursery win at Doncaster, so the talent’s definitely there. Still open to plenty of improvement and if he settles better, he’s got the class to be a big threat here.
Just 3 runs to date and won at Kempton on the 2nd run back in January of this year, crucially over the same distance (1m) as tomorrow, and does not look like one to be underestimated.

Twice a winner as a two-year-old, he returned to action over a mile at Kempton and showed improved form to finish 2nd, keeping on nicely. He should stay further, but another bold show is on the cards.
It's a competitive race, this one, with a few in with a shout. This one is the percentage call, though. It goes well here and was not beaten by far latest over C/D in a higher grade of race.
Kracking looks to be a sound each way bet in this. He has the speed, just needs to be held back a little longer based on his run at this venue a week ago.
Three times a course and distance winner, and last won last August off 76 at Lingfield. Huge chance back at his favourite track from a mark of just 70 and dropped into a 0-70 for the first time.

Super Hit hasn’t been at his best since that win here in October, and was well beaten at Southwell last time, but the cheekpieces go on now and the yard’s in good nick. Back at a track he’s won at and off a workable mark, there’s a chance he could bounce back if the headgear change sparks him up.

Firmly at the bottom of the handicap mark in this field, but is a C&D winner and looks to be moving in the right direction after an encouraging effort LTO when 4th of 11 last month. It can cause an upset if improvements are made despite the mark staying the same.

Aim For The Bull didn’t land a blow last time at Wolverhampton but was a bit short of room late on and might have needed the run. Looks like he’ll be better over further, so this step up should suit, and the yard’s in great form with a strong record in all-weather handicaps here (194 runs, 22 wins, 11% strike rate, +85pts @ 44% ROI). Could take a step forward now conditions look more in his favour.
Showed some improved form when switched to the all-weather here in February when finishing 2nd. Not as good at Southwell next time, but holds every chance back here if rediscovering February's form.

A weak-looking handicap where No Gain looks a decent punt at 15/2. He stepped up markedly on all previous form on his handicap debut at Wolves last month, and from the same mark again, can progress further to land this. The step down in trip looks a good move.

Daughter of Soldier's Call who was last seen at Wolverhampton 16 days ago where finishing 10th/11 however she is capable of shrugging off that latest effort and arrives here operating on a  basement mark of 47 now surely this daughter of Soldier's Call & Due Care ( Dam's sire Due Diligence ) is likely to better than a mark of 47 in very good time and can begin to make her presence felt the cheekpieces are applied for the first time here and they can have a positive effect this looks to be straightforward assignment for J Butler's inmate that looks pretty thin in nature and Due Respect can be whole different proposition this time out in a thin looking class 6 handicap has gate 1 here at Chelmsford that should put him in the perfect position with Jockey Lewis Edmunds taking the ride that being another positive factor . Respected .
